To avoid over penetration, your best bet is a caliber with low chamber pressure & a soft-lead bullet. 158g semi-wadcutter soft lead hollowpoints work great in a .38spc, as do various combinations of .45 cal hollowpoints. Soft lead bullets expand at lower velocities than harder lead compounds, and tend to get stuck in barriers like 2x4's and drywall as well.

High-pressure rounds like a .40 cal require significant velocity to expand, so it's a catch-22 for home defense. If the bullet's hollow point is clogged and doesn't expand, you're basically shooting through the intruder and into your walls. With a soft lead bullet, you'll get expansion with minimal barrier penetration no matter what.

A low-pressure round with a soft-lead bullet in the .40 could possibly do the trick, but would require hand loading, and feeding could be an issue.

For regular ammo, I'd suggest light-weight hollowpoint rounds, as I've seen heavier .40 cal (actually 10mm, same bullet) rounds fail to expand in relevant testing scenarios (Paul Harrel's meat target on YT). A 180g .40 cal hollowpoint may not expand due to insufficient velocity (and a relatively hard lead compound), so look for 160g bullets or less. Be sure to identify legitimate brands, as some hollowpoint brands don't perform well.

I'd suggest researching on YT and other sites where bullet tests in various mediums and vs. various barriers are conducted. Some HP ammo doesn't work very well, while other brands excel.
